question.text: Assertion: Object A is thrown straight upward from a point on the ground. At the same instant, object B is launched from a different point on the ground and follows a curved projectile path, as pictured. Object A comes back down to the ground after 4 seconds, and at that same instant object B lands on object A. For this to happen, the peak height H reached by B works out to be 20 m. (Take g = 10 m/s².) Reason: For this situation to occur, the two objects must be launched with equal speeds.

options.1: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options.2: If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options.3: If the Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options.4: If the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

conditions: A is thrown vertically upward from the ground
B is launched at the same instant along a curved projectile path from a different ground point
B lands on A exactly when A returns to the ground

figure.description: B starts from a point on the ground and follows a parabolic path that climbs to a peak height H before coming back down to ground level exactly at the point where A is thrown straight up from and returns to.

solution.approach: Particle A's flight time fixes its own launch speed; requiring B to land on A at the same instant fixes only B's vertical launch speed, not B's full speed.

steps.text: Particle A is thrown straight up and returns to the ground in 4 s, so find its launch speed from the time of flight.
Particle B collides with A at the instant A returns to the ground, so B is also in flight for 4 s.
Find the vertical component of B's launch velocity from its own time of flight, using the same relation as for A.
The maximum height of a projectile depends only on the vertical component of its launch velocity.
This confirms the Assertion: H = 20 m, and this value does not depend on B's horizontal launch speed, which the given data never fixes.
Because B's horizontal speed is unknown and generally nonzero, B's full launch speed need not equal A's 20 m/s, so the Reason is false even though the Assertion is true.
steps.why_this_step: Only the vertical launch component is pinned down by the 4 s flight time; the horizontal component is free.

final_answer.value: If the Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming B must be launched at exactly A's speed because the two particles meet at the same point at the same time, which makes the Reason look correct.
Accepting the Reason as u_B = 20 m/s and computing H = u_B² sin²θ/(2g), which is below 20 m for any angle under 90°, so wrongly rejecting the Assertion.
